$comment: The sigx ecosystem manifest — the single source of truth for WHICH repos consume core
and in WHAT ORDER they must be aligned and released after a core release.
(the orchestrator), and scripts/check-ecosystem.mjs (the CI guard that keeps it honest).
`tier` is the release wave. A repo's tier must be strictly greater than the tier of every
repo publishing a package it lists in `consumesSiblings` — check-ecosystem.mjs enforces
exactly that, so the ordering can never rot the way the hardcoded fan-out list did.
Everything in one tier can be aligned and released in parallel; the next tier may not
start until every package in the previous one is live on npm.
Deliberately absent: signalxjs/devtools (pins core ^0.5.0, v0.0.1, never published — a
rewrite, not a bump) and signalxjs/signalxjs.github.io (the docs agent's queue; file an
issue there per AGENTS.md, never a PR from a source repo).

consumers.publishesNote: zero-brutalist, zero-carbon, zero-heroui, zero-material and zero-ext-example are private (in-repo design systems and the extension fixture).
consumers.consumesNote: @sigx/zero-kit (the design-system toolchain) drives @sigx/cli + @sigx/args, which puts this repo above cli (tier 2). lynx pins @sigx/zero and @sigx/zero-daisyui at an exact prerelease (0.2.0-beta.N) — until zero ships a stable, every zero release is a lynx catalog bump. Missing from this manifest until #731: the v1.0.0 rollout's tier barrier never saw the edge, and lynx could not install (two core lines) until zero published against core 1.0.

consumers.publishesNote: 60+ @sigx/lynx-* packages ship from this repo, all lockstep-versioned; only the roots are listed. check-ecosystem.mjs treats `publishes` as a subset check for this repo.
consumers.consumesNote: @sigx/zero / @sigx/zero-daisyui are pinned EXACTLY (0.2.0-beta.N) in the catalog — the lynx-target emitters in @sigx/zero-kit must match the zero runtime byte-for-byte — so a zero release is a lynx catalog bump, not a range that resolves on its own. Tier 4 because zero is tier 3.

the package peers only `sigx` (and `mermaid`, a non-sigx peer). @sigx/server-renderer, @sigx/vite, @sigx/router and @sigx/ssg are examples-only — but examples/basic doubles as the e2e fixture, so a breaking change in any of them fails this repo's build. Hence the tier, not just the pins.
